questions.prompt: Pupils go to learn at ___. (A Home, B School, C Hospital)
steps: School is the intended learning institution.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: She was told to mop the ___. (A Flower, B Floor, C Flour)
steps: A floor is a surface that can be mopped.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I wear a cap ___ my head. (A Under, B On, C In)
steps: A cap rests on the head.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The ___ was roaring at midnight. (A Lion, B Elephant, C Donkey)
steps: A lion roars.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The teacher puts her books ___ the table. (A Under, B On, C In)
steps: On is the ordinary intended surface location; no picture restricts the place.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. On (intended); A. under is grammatical in another situation.

steps: Reorder d, i, r, b to b-i-r-d, using every letter once.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
G-o-a-t uses every printed letter; toga is a garment, so the anagram is not unique.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Goat (intended); toga is itself a valid word.

steps: T-a-b-l-e and b-l-e-a-t both use all the letters.

H-e-a-d uses every letter once.

questions.prompt: Write the young one of the pictured cat.
steps: The picture shows a cat; its young is a kitten.

questions.prompt: Write the young one of a lion.
steps: A young lion is a cub.

questions.prompt: Write the young one of a hen.
steps: A young chicken is a chick.

questions.prompt: According to the story, who is an artist?
steps: The passage names him as a good artist.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Kasongo get through his job?
steps: The final sentence says he gets money through his work.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Write the opposite of the underlined word good.
steps: The underlined adjective good has the antonym bad.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Dictation: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension and animal young: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.
